project.name: Reaper
project.scope: Flow-first programming language, Python reference runtime, developing native C17 core and developer tooling.

entries.acceptance: Reproduce the defect, isolate its root cause, add a regression check, and verify the corrected behavior at the affected entry point.
Check boundaries, units, tolerances, rounding and measurement assumptions from more than one independent path.
Remove the underlying cause across dependent components; do not hide symptoms with local workarounds.

entries.target: Module composition and public entry points
entries.acceptance: Close missing acceptance conditions across implementation, tests, documentation, configuration and distribution artifacts.

entries.target: CLI execution and end-to-end program flow
entries.acceptance: Exercise the complete user workflow, including invalid input, cancellation, failure and recovery branches.
Run deterministic diagnostics for supported platforms and configurations; report unsupported combinations explicitly.
Review functional behavior, security, resource use, accessibility, compatibility and documentation as one change set.
Measure a reproducible baseline before optimizing and prove that correctness, safety and output quality do not regress.

entries.target: CMake targets and CI build variants
entries.acceptance: Restructure components only with explicit interface contracts, migration notes and compatibility regression checks.

entries.target: Native C frontend and Python/native compatibility
entries.acceptance: Update toolchains, platforms and dependencies deliberately, then run the affected build and regression matrix.

entries.target: Polyglot adapters and supported source profiles
entries.acceptance: Synchronize supported profiles, operating modes, locales and configurations so they do not drift independently.

entries.target: Language feature audit and regression evidence
entries.acceptance: Audit implementation, tests, diagnostics, release workflows and evidence links; record findings with reproducible references.
Recover from partial failures without corrupting existing data; verify idempotency and atomicity where relevant.

entries.target: FFI, embedded ABI and trusted-code boundary
entries.acceptance: Keep defaults, thresholds, quotas, timeouts and policy boundaries consistent with the documented operating envelope.
Verify end-to-end conformance from the public interface through implementation and persisted/exported results.
Remove harmful duplication and dependency cycles while preserving public contracts and observable behavior.

entries.target: Resource quotas, memory accounting and cleanup
entries.acceptance: Contain failures with explicit upper bounds for memory, CPU, retries, input sizes and execution time.

entries.target: Federation contracts and imported project data
entries.acceptance: Resolve mismatches between source code, schemas, APIs, specifications, tests and user-facing documentation.
Use canonical data formats and versioned interfaces for shared capabilities without erasing project-specific boundaries.
Gate releases on relevant regression checks, clean build artifacts, synchronized documentation and reviewable evidence.

limitations: Evidence checks verify repository-relative file presence only; they do not execute or semantically validate the referenced implementation.
Passing this profile does not certify zero defects, security, hardware compatibility, language parity or commercial readiness.
The project's existing permissions, licensing, interoperability and safety boundaries remain authoritative.
